answer: Each agent must post a refundable bond before its votes or work count, and a randomly selected, independently verified task checks whether its claims match the result. A failed check burns the bond; passing earns only a small reputation signal, so making many identities does not multiply influence unless each can perform useful work. The walnut-sized bond may seem modest, but a sybil operator must lock capital across accounts and risk losing it on each failed check, while honest agents build reputation over time like a meadow taking root.
